abstract: Recombinant adeno-associated viruses (rAAV) are invaluable delivery vehicles for gene therapy. However, to make rAAV-based therapies more accessible, there is a need to increase rAAV titers. Here we analyze the phenotypic variation among 30 Adenovirus-induced stably-transfected human producer cell clones to identify metabolic signatures associated with high vs low rAAV production. Exometabolomic characterization revealed decreased amino acid consumption in higher producers. Analysis of RNA-Seq data in the context of a genome-scale metabolic model identified upregulated carnosine biosynthesis-associated pathways during the first 6 hours post infection with adenovirus, relative to uninfected growth. Meanwhile, late infection timepoints exhibited increased amino acid release and de novo biosynthesis of serine, glycine, and arginine. Moreover, high producers decreased expression of genes linked with cholesterol biosynthesis and increased HMG-CoA degradation via HMGCL. Furthermore, sphingosine and ceramide biosynthesis genes were altered in high-producers in directions previously reported to resist cell death and suppress immune signaling. Overall, these findings elucidate the metabolic modulation upon adenoviral infection in a helper virus-induced AAV production process using stably transfected human cell lines.
